action_trace.summary: Generated 12 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class design, SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter), pain points (current implementation gaps), and acceptance criteria. Questions target workflow enablement, user personas, architectural fit, and trade-off reasoning aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

Generated 10 targeted interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class design rationale), pain points (groups parameter handling, current alternatives), and acceptance criteria (usage patterns, success definitions). Questions decompose the sklearn_2021q4 requirement fragments into actionable clarifications grounded in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

Generated 10 interview questions targeting sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector abstract class requirement (Issue #21356) using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals, pain points, acceptance criteria, and design rationale while uncovering workflow constraints and trade-offs.

End-user requires abstract feature selector base class with consistent interface and groups parameter support in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() to enable production-grade automated ML pipelines that handle grouped/temporal data without leakage while supporting transparent strategy composition.

End-user confirms two critical pain points: (1) manual feature selection lacks standardized abstractions in sklearn, and (2) SequentialFeatureSelector cannot handle grouped data in fit(). Business expectations require abstract base class pattern for consistent selector interfaces and groups parameter support for stratified cross-validation in production workflows with structured data (time-series, cohorts, hierarchies).

End-user requires abstract base class for feature selectors with standardized interfaces and groups parameter support in fit() method to enable proper handling of grouped/stratified data in production ML workflows including time-series and hierarchical datasets.

Six clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities around: (1) ABC design scope and enforced interface, (2) groups parameter semantics and cv interaction, (3) pipeline composition model, (4) grouped data use cases and multi-level support, (5) backward compatibility requirements, and (6) automation vs. standardization intent for feature selection workflows.

Clarification questions targeting three ambiguous areas: (1) scope and interface contract of proposed abstract base class for feature selectors, (2) interaction semantics between groups and cv parameters in SequentialFeatureSelector, and (3) expected composition patterns (transformer vs. meta-selector) for pipeline integration in production ML workflows.

Seven clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities in scope (ABC coverage), semantics (groups parameter behavior), interface design (transformer vs. estimator), composition strategy (groups+cv interaction), and automation expectations. Chain-of-Thought identified conflicts between design abstraction and functional enhancement that require EndUser confirmation before proceeding to requirements modeling.

End user confirms need for feature selector ABC with standardized interfaces and Pipeline compatibility. SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() requires groups parameter for stratified/grouped data handling. Groups and cv parameters work together (groups defines stratification within splits). Selectors use transformer interface (fit/transform) for Pipeline composition. ABC supports both univariate and multivariate strategies. Refinements address pain points in manual selection and grouped cross-validation for production workflows.

End-user confirms need for abstract base class standardizing feature selector interfaces and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter for grouped data support. Groups parameter works with cv for stratified splitting; ABC supports both univariate/multivariate strategies with transformer interface for Pipeline compatibility.

End-user requirements validated and refined: (1) ABC for feature selectors with consistent fit/transform interfaces for Pipeline composition; (2) SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() must accept groups parameter (array-like, sklearn convention) for stratified data; (3) groups-cv parameter interaction confirmed—groups defines stratification within splits and takes precedence when both specified; (4) transformer interface required for Pipeline steps; (5) ABC scope covers both univariate and multivariate strategies. Requirements address pain points in manual feature selection and grouped data handling in production workflows.

Consolidated 5 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue addressing abstract base class standardization for feature selectors (REQ-001), groups parameter addition to SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() with stratification semantics (REQ-002, REQ-005), Pipeline composition support (REQ-003), and multivariate selection coverage (REQ-004). All confirmations and validations integrated; requirements aligned to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 documentation standards with MoSCoW prioritization applied.

Six hierarchical user requirements synthesized from sklearn_2021q4 case addressing feature selection standardization (REQ-001: ABC for selectors; REQ-002/003: groups parameter in SequentialFeatureSelector with precedence logic) and pipeline composition (REQ-004/005/006). Two MUST requirements establish core abstractions; two SHOULD enable composition patterns; one COULD improves consistency. All traced to validated enduser confirmations and interview records.

Probed deployer on backward compatibility constraints, memory/performance scalability limits for groups parameter in cross-validation, security risks around data leakage in grouped scenarios, Pipeline composition patterns, regulatory compliance requirements (HIPAA/GDPR), edge case handling for unequal groups, caching/lazy evaluation trade-offs, and release cycle strategy to inform infrastructure-aware requirement refinement.

Formulated seven targeted questions probing sklearn's deployment infrastructure, security/governance mandates, scalability expectations, backward compatibility constraints, downstream integration dependencies, validation requirements, and resource/timeline constraints to inform concrete ABC design decisions and groups parameter implementation strategy.

Targeted dialogue probing Deployer's infrastructure constraints (environment/compute/versioning), security mandates (data governance/auditability), and scalability expectations (dataset size/group cardinality/distribution frameworks) to ground ABC design and groups parameter implementation in operational realities.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for ABC-based feature selector framework with groups parameter support: requires Python 3.8+/sklearn 1.x integration, in-memory processing up to 10GB, numpy array validation, groups-precedence-over-cv logic with backward compatibility, and parallel cross-validation support via joblib. No additional infrastructure investment needed; implementation effort ~2-3 sprints.

Deployer confirms scikit-learn 1.x+ infrastructure with backward-compatible ABC integration, 10GB in-memory scalability via numpy optimization, groups parameter validation with immutability enforcement, and groups-takes-precedence logic for fold structure definition. Cross-validation integration via GroupKFold wrapper, graceful fallback mechanisms, and ~5-10% acceptable performance overhead for production stratified data support.

Deploy feature selector ABC within scikit-learn 1.x+ with groups parameter support, ensuring backward compatibility, efficient numpy-based processing for 10GB datasets, O(1) group label lookup for 1000+ groups, strict input validation, and groups-parameter precedence logic in SequentialFeatureSelector.fit().

Six critical clarifications raised on ABC design scope, groups validation strategy, cross-validation performance optimization, Pipeline interface completeness, backward compatibility constraints, and groups-cv parameter interaction semantics to resolve ambiguities blocking deployment-ready implementation.

Deployer raises 8 critical clarifications on ABC method signatures, groups parameter validation strictness, fold pre-computation strategy, Pipeline return types, groups-cv precedence implementation, backward compatibility scope, security validation depth, and performance baselines—all necessary to resolve ambiguities between optional/mandatory groups parameters, memory-latency trade-offs, and integration constraints with existing sklearn 1.x+ infrastructure.

Deployer requires 8 operational clarifications to resolve ambiguities in ABC method signature enforcement, groups parameter validation strictness, fold pre-computation trade-offs, parameter precedence logic, pipeline interface scope, strategy support patterns, security validation boundaries, and backward compatibility constraints. These clarifications are critical for infrastructure deployment decisions affecting memory/latency trade-offs, error handling rigor, and sklearn integration compatibility.

Deployer confirms ABC implementation with optional groups parameter, strict validation (len matching + sanitization), pre-computed fold boundaries for deterministic performance, and groups-over-cv precedence logic. Refines univariate/multivariate support via optional abstract methods and optimizes 1000+ group label scaling through hash-based indexing. Validates scikit-learn 1.x+ integration with zero breaking changes, 10GB in-memory support, and immutable groups array handling for production deployment.

Deployer confirms ABC implementation with optional groups parameter, strict validation (length matching + type checking), pre-computed fold boundaries, and O(1) group lookup optimization. Groups parameter takes precedence over cv when both specified. Feature selectors support transformer interface for Pipeline composition. Deployment targets sklearn 1.x+ with zero breaking changes; scales to 1000+ group labels and 10GB datasets. Security validated through array sanitization and immutability enforcement.

Deployer confirms ABC implementation with optional groups parameter (backward compatible), strict array validation (length matching + numpy type-checking), pre-computed fold boundaries for deterministic performance, and groups-takes-precedence logic when combined with cv parameter. Infrastructure targets sklearn 1.x+ (Python 3.8+), supports 10GB in-memory datasets, scales to 1000+ group labels, and enables Pipeline composition with transformer interface. Security validated through sanitization and injection prevention; cost-performance trade-off accepted for production reliability.

Operating environment specification for sklearn 1.x+ (Python 3.8+) feature selector ABC implementation: in-memory processing up to 10GB with numpy-optimized groups parameter handling; strict validation with length matching and injection attack prevention; optional groups parameter in fit(X, y, groups=None) signature with precedence over cv; pre-computed fold boundaries for deterministic performance; hash-based O(1) group lookup for 1000+ labels; Pipeline composition support with transformer interface; backward compatibility maintained across all selector classes.

Consolidated system requirements for sklearn feature selector enhancement (Q4 2021): establish abstract base class enforcing standardized fit/transform interfaces with optional groups parameter for stratified cross-validation, implement groups validation with strict length matching and O(1) lookup performance for 1000+ labels, pre-compute fold boundaries during fit() initialization, and enable Pipeline composition—all while maintaining backward compatibility with Python 3.8+ and scikit-learn 1.x+ without breaking changes.

Selected SysML Block Definition Diagram (BDD) with parametric constraints as primary modeling methodology to decompose multi-faceted sklearn feature selector architecture spanning ABC interface standardization, groups parameter validation, cross-validation fold pre-computation, and pipeline composition. Supplemented with UML Sequence Diagram (groups parameter workflow) and UML Class Diagram (ABC inheritance hierarchy) to capture temporal dependencies and inheritance contracts. SysML notation enables explicit modeling of method signatures, parameter constraints, and composition relationships critical for enforcing consistency across six system requirements while maintaining backward compatibility with sklearn 1.x+ ecosystem.

SRS evaluation against ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 identified 10 defects: 3 clarity violations (undefined selector scope, incomplete validation spec, ambiguous transform return type), 2 feasibility concerns (heterogeneous group label types, sklearn backend ambiguity), 2 consistency violations (cv parameter precedence conflict, redundant requirements), 2 traceability gaps (untraceable memory budget, undefined lazy evaluation constraint), 1 verifiability defect (missing default behavior for groups+cv interaction). Highest-severity issues: SRS-004 precedence logic conflict and SRS-006 transform() return type ambiguity require immediate clarification before implementation.

All six SRS findings resolved through requirement clarification: ABC scope defined for sklearn.feature_selection module; groups parameter type handling standardized with int/str normalization; error validation completed with comprehensive NaN/None checks; precedence logic conflict eliminated; fold pre-computation traceability established with memory/performance quantification; pipeline composition return types finalized with sklearn compatibility validation. Closure confirmed for sklearn_2021q4 requirements development cycle.
